description: The last Concorde built and the last to fly, landing at Filton on 26 November 2003 and now the centrepiece of the museum in its own purpose-built hangar.
Canadian-built Blenheim, ex-Royal Canadian Air Force. Long-running volunteer restoration; wings, tail cone and tailplane refitted by 2026.
Forward fuselage section only, recovered and conserved as an exhibit; displayed inside.

Ex-Royal New Zealand Air Force Bristol Freighter, previously ZK-EPG; shipped to the UK in 2017. One of about twelve survivors and the only one in Europe. Moved outdoors in July 2026 as conservation continues.
Nose section only of the second Britannia prototype G-ALRX, written off at Littleton-on-Severn in 1954 and later converted into a simulator. Serial VX447 was allotted but not taken up.
The first British twin-rotor helicopter, first flown 3 January 1952; also carried the civil registration G-ALBN. Ex-maintenance serial 7648M.
RAF Sycamore, ex-maintenance serial 8021M; previously at the Manchester Museum of Science and Industry and the RAF Museum store at Stafford before arriving at Filton in April 2015.
Airlifted to the museum site by RAF Chinook in September 2015. Wears 800 and 801 Naval Air Squadron markings and the codes L-000 and R-126.
aliases: Sea Harrier FA2; FRS2; SHAR; L-000; L000

description: Flying replica built in 1964 for the film 'Those Magnificent Men in Their Flying Machines'; not an original airframe.
Replica of the Bristol Scout single-seat WWI scout, displayed in the World War One exhibit.
Original Bristol Fighter airframe frame suspended above a full replica in the World War One exhibit of the Heritage Hangar.
Replica of the 1919 Bristol Babe single-seat ultralight biplane.
